title: Scenarios and Goal Seek (Calc)
short: Data consolidation, subtotals, what-if scenarios, Goal Seek and Solver.
lede: The analysis half of Calc. Goal Seek is the one tool you must be able to demo.
lens: **Goal Seek** and **Scenarios** are the theory + practical pair.
concepts: **1. Consolidate:** Data → Consolidate. Combines the same layout from several sheets (e.g. four term marks) using Sum/Average. Tick “Link to source data” to auto-update.
**2. Groups and outline:** Data → Group and Outline. Hide detail rows; show only totals.
**3. Subtotals:** sort first, then Data → Subtotals on a column (e.g. subtotal marks by section).
**4. What-if analysis:** change inputs to see outputs. Three tools: Scenarios, Goal Seek, Solver.
**5. Scenarios:** named sets of input cells (Best case, Worst case). Tools → Scenarios. Switching the name swaps the inputs and the formulas recalculate.
**6. Goal Seek:** Tools → Goal Seek. You know the **result** you want; Calc finds the **input**. Example: “What price makes profit = 10000?” Set cell, To value, By changing cell.
**7. Solver:** for many variables and constraints (maximise profit with limits). Heavier than Goal Seek.
steps: 3. Formula cell already filled; type the target in “To value”.
5. OK — Calc tries values until the target is hit.
formulas: Goal Seek: set formula cell → target value → change input cell
tricks: - Goal Seek needs a **formula** in the set cell. Typing a number there will fail.
- Sort **before** Subtotals or the groups will be wrong.
mistakes: - Mixing up Goal Seek (one input) with Solver (many inputs + constraints).
- Forgetting to name scenarios, so you cannot switch back.

qa.q: What is Goal Seek in Calc?
qa.a: A what-if tool: you set the result you want in a formula cell and Calc finds the input value that produces it.

qa.q: What is a scenario?
qa.a: A named set of values for specified cells so you can switch between cases (best/worst) without retyping.

qa.q: Differentiate Consolidate and Subtotals.
qa.a: Consolidate **combines several ranges/sheets** into one summary (often another sheet). Subtotals **insert summary rows inside one sorted list** (sum of each group). Consolidate is across blocks; Subtotals is inside a table.

qa.q: A shop wants profit of ₹8,000. Profit is `=B2*B3-B4` (price × qty − cost). Which tool, and which cell is “By changing” if qty and cost are fixed?
qa.a: Goal Seek. Set cell = profit, To value = 8000, By changing = price (`B2`).

(b) Function Sum; add each range; Link to source data.
(c) Manual totals go stale; a link updates and reduces typing errors.

title: Macros in Spreadsheet
short: Record, run, and use macros as functions; when not to use them.
lede: Recording a macro is a 5-mark practical if you can find the menu under Tools.
lens: Steps to **record and run** a macro, plus one use-case (repeating a format or a formula block).
Security: enable macros only from trusted files.
concepts: **1. A macro** is a recorded sequence of commands. Play it back to repeat the work.
**2. Record:** Tools → Macros → Record Macro → do the steps → Stop Recording → name it → save in the document or My Macros.
**3. Run:** Tools → Macros → Run Macro → pick the name. Or assign it to a button / key.
**4. Use as a function:** some recorded macros can be called from a sheet; in Class 10 the expected skill is record-and-run, not writing BASIC by hand.
**5. Good uses:** apply a school marksheet format, insert a header, convert a column to uppercase, print settings.
**6. Macro security:** Tools → Options → Security → Macro Security. Very high / High / Medium / Low. Use Medium or High; never run macros from unknown people.
steps: 4. Tools → Macros → Run Macro to test.
5. Optional: assign to a toolbar button.
tricks: - Plan the clicks **before** you press Record — extra clicks get recorded too.
- Save the file as `.ods` with macros enabled; some formats drop macros.
mistakes: - Recording a macro that depends on a **specific cell** when you needed a relative range.
- Enabling macros on a downloaded file you do not trust.

qa.q: What is a macro? Give one use in Calc.
qa.a: A saved list of commands that can be replayed. Use: apply the same marksheet formatting every term.

qa.q: Write the menu path to record a macro in Calc.
qa.a: Tools → Macros → Record Macro, perform the steps, Stop Recording, name the macro.

qa.q: Explain macro security levels and a safe practice for students.
qa.a: Very High / High / Medium / Low control whether unsigned macros run. Students should keep High or Medium, enable macros only on their own practical files, and never open a macro-enabled sheet from an unknown chat.

qa.q: Every Monday you set print area A1:G40, landscape, header “Weekly Sales”. How does a macro help?
qa.a: Record those page-setup steps once. Each Monday, Run Macro — one click instead of eight menu steps, fewer missed settings.

qa.q:
Read and answer:

A classmate sends `marks.ods` that auto-runs a macro on open.

(a) What should you do first?
(b) When is a macro a good idea in your own file?
(c) One limitation of recorded macros.
a: (a) Do not enable macros until you trust the source; check Security level.
(b) When the same clicks are repeated often on your own data.
(c) They record extra clicks; they may break if the sheet layout changes.

title: Linking Spreadsheet Data
short: Sheet links, hyperlinks, linking to external files and data from the web.
lede: One formula across sheets is the whole idea: `'Sheet2'.A1` or a hyperlink to a file.
lens: Syntax of a sheet reference and Insert → Hyperlink.
External link: `'file:///path/file.ods'#Sheet1.A1` in principle; in the exam they ask the idea, not the URL.
concepts: **1. Same-file sheet link:** `=Sheet2.B3` or `='Term 1'.B3` if the sheet name has a space.
**2. Why link:** one source of truth — change the source, every summary updates.
**3. Hyperlink:** Insert → Hyperlink to a web page, a mail, a file, or a target in this document (a named cell).
**4. Linking to another spreadsheet:** copy cells → Paste Special → Link, or type an external reference. The target file should stay in the same folder for the practical exam.
**5. Data from the web / register:** Insert → Link to External Data (where available) for tables that refresh.
**6. Find broken links:** Edit → Links to External Files (if present) to update or break the link.
tricks: - Sheet names with spaces need **single quotes**: `'Term 1'.A1`.
mistakes: - Renaming a sheet after writing formulas without checking — some links break.
- Emailing only the summary file when it **links** to `data.ods` left on the lab PC.

qa.q: Write a formula that shows cell B4 of sheet Fees on sheet Summary.
What is a hyperlink in Calc?
qa.a: A clickable link to a web page, file, email or a location in the document, inserted via Insert → Hyperlink.

qa.q: Why is linking sheets better than copy-pasting values for a yearly total?
qa.a: A link stays live: when a term sheet changes, the year sheet updates. Copy-paste values go stale, cause mismatch, and make auditing harder.

qa.q: Summary sheet must show `Total` from three term sheets named Term1, Term2, Term3, each total in G20. Write the formula.

Read and answer:

A student pastes last month’s numbers into the annual sheet. The teacher later corrects the January file; the annual sheet does not change.

(a) What did the student do wrong?
(b) How should the cells have been pasted?
(c) One risk of live links.

(b) Paste Special → Link, or a formula to the January sheet.
(c) If the source file is moved/renamed, the link breaks — keep files together.

title: Share and Review a Spreadsheet
short: Sharing, recording changes, adding comments, comparing and merging sheets.
lede: The collaboration half of Calc — same idea as Track Changes in Writer.
lens: Share spreadsheet + record changes is the pair.
concepts: **1. Share spreadsheet:** Tools → Share Spreadsheet. Several people can open it (on a network). Conflicts are resolved when saving.
**2. Record changes:** Edit → Track Changes → Record (wording may be Record Changes). Shows who changed which cell.
**3. Show changes:** Edit → Track Changes → Show. Accept or reject like Writer.
**4. Comments on cells:** Insert → Comment. A small triangle marks the cell. Use for “please check this total”, not for storing the answer itself.
**5. Compare documents:** Edit → Track Changes → Compare Document — against an older copy to see differences.
**6. Merge:** bring another user’s copy back into the shared original.
**7. Protect sheet:** Tools → Protect Sheet so others can edit only unlocked input cells.
tricks: - Sharing is for **one file, many users**; emailing five copies is how totals diverge.
- Unlock input cells **before** protecting the sheet.
mistakes: - Protecting the sheet with no password written in the practical file — you cannot demo it.
- Recording changes after the work is already done.

qa.q: How do you share a Calc spreadsheet?
qa.a: Tools → Share Spreadsheet → enable sharing. Save on a network location the team can open.

qa.q: Why add a comment to a cell instead of changing the value?
qa.a: A comment suggests or questions without overwriting data; the original number stays until someone decides.

qa.q: Explain recording, showing and accepting changes in Calc.
qa.a: Turn Record on before editing. Each changed cell is marked. Show lists author, date and old/new value. Accept keeps the new value; Reject restores the old. Compare Document does this against a saved copy.

qa.q: Three lab partners type in three copies of `stock.ods` and the totals disagree. What should they have used?
qa.a: One shared spreadsheet (or one file with Record Changes + merge), not three independent copies.
